A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same behavior-targeted reinforcement-learning attack framework, although v2 renames the attack and expands the work to defense. Both versions' main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Meta-World attack experiments and a parking trajectory case study in Section 6, plus pruning and demonstration-size experiments in Appendices D and G.

after.justification: v2 reports original attack and defense experiments on Meta-World, MuJoCo and MiniGrid, together with sensitivity analyses and training-time measurements in Section 7 and Appendices F–I.

M1.justification: The imitation-based attack core remains under the new name BIA. Substantive changes include the new TDRT defense, which adds time-discounted policy-sensitivity regularization to PPO, and removal of v1's gradient-based structured-pruning procedure for selecting attacked state dimensions.

E1.justification: v2 adds handle-press-side and handle-pull-side to the eight retained Meta-World tasks. It adds Ant, HalfCheetah and Hopper locomotion tasks and MiniGrid navigation with coordinate and RGB observations, including reward-increase attacks on deliberately limited-performance victims. The Highway-env Parking trajectory-following experiment is removed.

E2.justification: v2 retains Random and the reward-maximizing SA-RL comparator, and adds Targeted PGD and reward-maximizing PA-AD to the Meta-World comparison. New defense comparisons evaluate ATLA-PPO, PA-ATLA-PPO, RAD-PPO, WocaR-PPO and SA-PPO against TDRT. The magnitude-based pruning comparison disappears with the pruning study.

E3.justification: The principal experiments change from SAC victims and attack success rates to PPO victims and cumulative attack rewards. Demonstrations increase from eight to twenty episodes, and evaluation changes from thirty to fifty episodes. Perturbation-budget and demonstration-size sweeps are revised, while new defense experiments introduce clean-reward and maximum-attack-reward evaluations.

E4.justification: v2 revises the existing demonstration-size and attack-budget analyses and adds target-policy-quality experiments, regularization-strength comparisons, time-discounting comparisons, training-efficiency analysis and Targeted PGD sensitivity analysis. It also investigates image-input failure. v1's pruning-sensitivity analysis and parking trajectory case study are removed.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports five trials and standard deviations across five seeds. v2 reports means and standard deviations over fifty evaluation episodes, with half-standard-deviation bands in Figures 3–5, but gives no training-seed count. This substantially changes the reported source of variability without establishing how many training runs were performed.

E6.justification: v1's success-rate results are replaced by reward results under changed settings. v2 Table 1 shows mixed rankings: BIA-ILfD versus SA-RL yields 3962 versus 4505 on window-close, but 3031 versus 1448 on faucet-open. Extensive defense, additional-environment, sensitivity and timing results are new. These are newly reported outcomes, not directly comparable cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds Theorem 5.1's variational-divergence reformulation and Theorem 6.1's time-weighted KL bound, with proofs in Appendix B. v1's Proposition 2 attack-effectiveness bound is removed. The earlier arbitrary-reward MDP lemma and distribution-matching result remain as Lemma B.1 and Theorem C.1, with revised compactness reasoning for the latter.

C1.justification: The paper's central contribution expands from an attack method to an attack-and-defense framework. v2 newly claims the first defense specifically designed for behavior-targeted attacks and claims improved original-task performance while preserving robustness. The attack-performance claim changes from outperforming baselines to competing with attacks possessing greater access or knowledge.

C2.justification: v1 explains weaker ILfO performance through missing action information; v2 attributes similar ILfD/ILfO performance to deterministic transitions. v2 adds explanations involving early-trajectory sensitivity, policy expressiveness, PGD's short planning horizon and imitation-induced locomotion disruption. Its limitations now explicitly address high-dimensional image inputs and TDRT's lack of certified guarantees, replacing defense as future work.

D1.justification: v2 adds hyperparameter-search ranges and selection criteria, auto_LiRPA and gradient-handling details for TDRT, Targeted PGD implementation instructions, H100 timing information and a stated code-access link. v1's fixed hyperparameter tables and several explicit training settings are no longer supplied. Reproducibility documentation is substantially revised rather than uniformly expanded.

R1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A substantially expand positioning against policy smoothing, adversarial training, certified defenses, regret-based learning, poisoning and newer behavior-targeted attacks by Bai et al. v2 also distinguishes its proof and reward construction from earlier MDP-based ideas and positions TDRT as a specialized defense.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten around attack and defense. Related work becomes a standalone main section, preliminaries are condensed, attack mathematics moves into appendices, and the appendix organization is rebuilt. SAIA becomes BIA, and the author and affiliation text also changes.

P2.justification: The principal presentation changes from success-rate plots and a parking visualization to attack, robustness and clean-reward tables. v2 adds an SA-MDP schematic, extensive defense tables and new analysis plots. Demonstration-size plots change axes and panel organization; pruning plots and fixed hyperparameter tables disappear. These are substantial display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 adds a substantial defense investigation, broader empirical coverage and informative failure cases. However, central new evidence is inconsistent: Table 8 reports TDRT's best attack reward as 1928 for handle-press-side despite listing an SA-RL reward of 4067 in that row. Algorithm 2 also adds the KL regularizer during gradient ascent, conflicting with Equation 12's penalty. Together with the loss of explicit seed-level variability reporting, these unresolved issues prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
